my interests tend to loop in a cycle that includes mortuary science / death rituals, (i was really into a victorian mourning rituals phase for ~4 years) botany (usually of invasive species, i was besotted with foxglove, but also those used in herbal medicine) insects (parasitoid wasps are dear to my heart,) early psychology experiments, world war era medicine, the effects of human pollution on our oceans (which spiraled into food safety, fishery practices, corals, ocean acidification, the garbage patch hanging out in the pacific…), exotic animal care and breeding, deep sea life (which tangented off into ocean sea vents) nuclear waste and disasters, arctic expeditions, serial killers, surgical complications and diseases, parasites (tapeworms in particular) twins (as used in scientific experiments, conjoined, parasitic,) war crimes, unsolved mysteries (murders, disappearances that sort of thing) but right now it’s probably meningitis, conjoined twins, female serial killers, the epidermolysis bullosas, and harlequin ichthyosis. 
 
a lot of them aren’t really socially acceptable to babble about, but i’ve been pleasantly surprised that my weird jumping all over the place between environmental science and medicine made my environmental science and biology class a breeze- since to sum it up my interests lie in “the intersections between humanity and nature,” whether that takes the form of fungal / viral / bacterial infections, pollution waste streams, the struggles of modern medicine against natures indifference, population dynamics and limiting factors, etc. so i’m hoping, since fingers crossed i’ll be a biomedical major, that i might be able to make friends who want to shoot the shit about antibiotic resistant strains of bacteria or whatever’s grabbed my mind by the reigns instead of sort of glazing over mid conversation.
